problem_addressed: Moldova counted many services as digital while few were fully digital and many were unused: a 2023 brief found 36 of 157 services that could be requested online were provided in digital format, and 128 of the 226 services reported as digital had no users in 2022. The Commission still named low demand, especially in rural areas, as limiting use of e-government services in its 2025 report.
reform_or_mechanism: The main measures are the World Bank-financed Modernization of Government Services project run by the e-Governance Agency, the Public Services Portal, the EVO app launched in June 2024, assisted access through Unified Public Service Centres (CUPS), and a strategy approved in September 2023 with digitalisation targets. The approach is service-by-service digitalisation with assisted access. No item records a legal duty on institutions or users to use one portal.
how_implemented: Offered: the Commission reports 15 online services launched on the electronic services platform in its 2024 report and two in 2025, and over 50% of mapped services available 'fully or partially'. Fully transactional: the only figure with a stated definition is the 2023 brief's 36 of 157, because the agency's 283 e-services include partly automated ones and its 303 of 648 'fully digitalized' (2025) and 445 of 636 'accessed digitally' (2026) are unverified. EVO lists all services 'regardless of how they are provided', so a listing there is not a transaction. The Commission confirms 105 CUPS, but no source says how many people they served.
evidence_of_results: Used: the 2022 service-level data show 128 of 226 digital services with no users, 77 of them with requests at counters and 51 with no requests on any channel, and this count has not been repeated. The agency's survey reports online access passing offline access (54.5% against 52.6%), and the agency reports 71% of 4.5 million requests submitted online in January to June 2026, up 7 points on 2025. The Commission states that access and use 'significantly increased', with no figure and no named cause. No item measures use of the Public Services Portal or EVO themselves.
limitations_of_evidence: Every use figure after 2023 comes from the agency, a survey it commissioned or the project's funder, and no independent check was found; the request series does not say which services it counts. The rise from 25% to over 54% of citizens has no stated base, and a similar 2023 survey figure is reported for people who used public services, not all citizens. Blocked sources, including the SIGMA 2024 reports, are a recorded gap (LIM-0028). Use figures are listed as outcome items here although pass 2 classed them as implementation, because use is the result this issue asks about.
practical_lesson_for_north_macedonia: North Macedonia's stated mechanism includes low uptake of a working portal (MEC-11), with 292,179 users and 2,070 monthly applications in 2024. Moldova supports the narrow point that a count of digital services says little about use, since more than half of those reported for 2022 had no users, although 51 of the 128 had no demand on any channel. It also shows reported use rising alongside service redesign and assisted access, but it does not show which measure raised it.
transferable: Counting use service by service, and separating fully from partly digital services, does not depend on Moldova's context and would address North Macedonia's conflicting service counts. Assisted access answers a barrier also planned for in North Macedonia's DigInfo centres, but its effect on use is unmeasured, so it transfers only as an idea to test.
not_transferable: The Moldovan results sit within a seven-year donor project and a dedicated agency, while North Macedonia's ownership is described as fragmented, with 101 of 242 foreseen posts unfilled. Moldova runs several front ends whose relationship the sources do not state, so it offers no tested single-portal model. North Macedonia's increase in e-services is a Reform Agenda condition, and no item shows the same condition for Moldova; relative size was not assessed because no item gives it.
can_be_attributed: The outputs (110 digitalised services, 94 redesigned services and seven new platforms) can be attributed to the project on the agency's own account, as outputs only. The Commission's statement that CUPS provide rural access to e-services can be attributed to the CUPS measure as access, not as use.
cannot_be_attributed: The rise in online use cannot be attributed to the project, EVO, CUPS or the strategy, because no source tests it and the link rests on statements made at the project's closing event. The reported savings (30 billion and 10 billion lei, and the recovery of 46 million dollars through MPay) have no stated method and concern cost, not use of the portal.
description: Moldova digitalised services through a long donor-backed project and assisted access, and reports online use rising, with service-level data for 2022 showing most digital services unused. The rise rests on agency and funder reporting, and no source shows what caused it.

problem_addressed: Albania's gap is depth and inclusion more than range: the Commission records 95% of applications for 1,237 services offered online in 2024 and 1,253 in 2025, yet accessibility for vulnerable groups remains unaddressed. It also asks Albania to improve access to the use of e-services and to address an emerging digital divide. The national monitor finds digitalisation largely complete but citizens not at the centre of design and delivery.
reform_or_mechanism: Law No. 43/2023 on Electronic Governance, adopted in June 2023, requires public institutions to use e-Albania as the primary point of access and requires e-payment through the portal; as stated in the sources, the duty falls on institutions, not users. The Digital Agenda 2022-2026 sets a 95% target. ADISA was absorbed by the National Agency for Information Society, which concentrates policy and operational control.
how_implemented: Offered: the monitor records more than 90% of services placed on the portal since its previous cycle and most physical counters closed, while municipal offices still handle services that need in-person steps. Fully transactional: no source gives a national count, and of seven sampled services the monitor calls two end-to-end, while its own footnote says the payment option usually does not work, and others, such as vehicle registration and VAT, need in-person payment. No service is yet delivered as a life event. Vehicle registration and VAT are described as offered outside the portal in one passage and as sampled services needing in-person payment in another.
evidence_of_results: Used: the Regional Cooperation Council (RCC) reports e-government users at 78.5% of internet users in 2023 and 88.6% in 2024, with 3.43 million registered users and 15.2 million services provided in 2024 and 17 million in 2025. The monitor's perception survey has 66.9% agreeing that they can access services easily online and 30.5% disagreeing. No source gives the share of those services that were completed online from start to finish.
limitations_of_evidence: The RCC gives no origin for the portal figures and does not define a registered user or a service provided; its text says 89% of the population where its table says 88.6% of internet users. The e-government user indicator counts any online contact with authorities, not portal use. There is no series from before the June 2023 law, so use before and after it cannot be compared. The monitor's informant scores are points awarded only if all informants agree (0 of 3 on accessible service delivery, 3 of 3 on ease of use), so they are not counts of people.
practical_lesson_for_north_macedonia: North Macedonia's 2025 strategy proposes updating the law towards mandatory integration of each e-service on the portal, and its stated mechanisms include coordination failure (MEC-08) and low uptake (MEC-11). Albania shows that a duty on institutions can sit alongside most services being placed on one portal and high reported use, but no source shows that the duty caused either, and the legal e-payment duty is reported as limited in practice. The case does not support the claim that a mandate drives use; it supports, at most, the RCC's untested statement that uptake is linked to the portal's central role.
transferable: Concentrating responsibility in one body answers North Macedonia's fragmented ownership, and the monitor states that this resolved institutional overlaps in Albania. A legal duty on institutions to integrate services could address range, on condition that it is enforced and that payment and signature work in practice, which Albania's experience shows cannot be assumed.
not_transferable: Closing counters cannot be assumed to transfer: the source gives no count, date or effect on users, and North Macedonia has 1,120 services available only in person and an audit finding that persons with disabilities cannot use e-services. Albania's own unaddressed accessibility issues show that its route has not solved this. Relative size was not assessed because no item gives it. In these items the Commission's ask of Albania is a recommendation, while North Macedonia's increase in e-services is also a Reform Agenda condition.
can_be_attributed: That services are delivered through the portal can be attributed to the portal only as a channel, since the count is of services through it. The monitor states that absorbing ADISA resolved institutional overlaps, which is an institutional result and not a result on use.
cannot_be_attributed: Reported use cannot be attributed to Law No. 43/2023: no source links the two, and the RCC's link names the portal's central role, with no test and no mention of the law. Portal consolidation, the law, closed counters and pre-filled forms cannot be separated, and no source says how far use reflects choice and how far the absence of a counter.
description: Albania placed most services on e-Albania, with a 2023 law obliging institutions to use it, and an international source reports high use. Full transactions are not established, payment often fails, and no source shows that the law or the portal caused the reported use.

problem_addressed: Montenegro's government names low use of e-services and weak interoperability as key challenges, and the Commission repeatedly asks it to prioritise a platform for transactional services. The national monitor, citing the government's own plan, finds no service at the fifth level (full online service). E-government users were 37.5% of internet users in 2024, below the Western Balkans average of 54%.
reform_or_mechanism: A new eUprava portal was launched in December 2024, with first services published in April 2025, under a plan for transactional services 2025-2027 covering 171 services and 21 institutions, revised on 18 December 2025. The Law on Electronic Government gives the legal basis, and the government launched an initiative for all institutions to publish their services on the portal. A proposed Open Government action plan targets 150 transactional services by 2029.
how_implemented: Offered: the government reports 106 services from 14 institutions on the portal, without saying how many are transactional, and eFirma and eTaxis run outside it. Fully transactional: the government states 45 transactional services now, while the monitor finds none at level 5, and the two are not reconciled. Delivery against the plan was 25 of 57 by July 2025, then 57 of 57 on the government's own report, which has no independent check. The ministry reports two officials in the responsible directorate, a refusal of budget reserve for Interior services and Employment Agency services waiting on a new law.
evidence_of_results: Used: e-government users fell from 48.4% of internet users in 2023 to 37.5% in 2024, on an indicator of any online contact with authorities, and an oral UNDP figure puts actual use at 8%. No item gives use of eUprava itself. The monitor finds the portal improved information for users but did not improve the service delivery grades, because none of the seven sampled services was on it. The government states that satisfaction is around 50%.
limitations_of_evidence: The portal is young and the independent monitor closes during 2025, before the government's report of full delivery for that year, so that report and the 106 count are untested. The RCC text says use continues to grow, against the fall in its own table. The 8% figure is oral, second-hand and has no reference period, and the event report is rated Low. The 2024 user figures predate almost all of the portal's life, so they measure the starting position.
practical_lesson_for_north_macedonia: Montenegro is the closest parallel to North Macedonia's position of a live portal, the most-needed services absent and capacity gaps (MEC-03, MEC-11), and it is a stalled case so far. It supports the narrow lesson that launching a portal without moving the most-needed services onto it can improve information without improving the service, which is the monitor's own finding. It also shows why a plan's delivered count needs an independent check on whether services are transactional, given North Macedonia's own conflicting counts.
transferable: The underlying mechanism applies directly: a portal adds little where the services people need sit elsewhere, and North Macedonia's Commission findings say the most commonly requested services are not yet online. The stated constraints of too few staff and refused budget have a parallel in North Macedonia's unfilled posts and limited resources for the ministry.
not_transferable: The Montenegrin portal launched in December 2024, while North Macedonia's has run since 2019 and has a longer record of low use, so results at Montenegro's stage may not predict results at a later one. Montenegro's 2023 cybersecurity crisis, which the Commission says delayed services and eroded trust, has no stated equivalent in North Macedonia's evidence here. Montenegro's different accession stage was not used as a reason, because no item links it to the portal.
can_be_attributed: The improvement in service information can be attributed to the portal on the monitor's account, since the information is published there. The government attributes over 45 services and the portal to the EU-funded COVID-19 project, which holds as an output claim only.
cannot_be_attributed: The fall in e-government users cannot be attributed to the portal, which launched at the end of the period measured. The Commission's 'no noticeable improvement' is as of the end of 2023, before this portal's launch, so it does not assess eUprava. The plan's 57 delivered services cannot be read as any change for users.
description: Montenegro launched a new portal in December 2024 and a plan for transactional services, but sampled core services were not on it and use on the broad indicator fell before it launched. This is a stalled case whose delivery figures rest on the government's own report.
